problem: Existing EQA methods (e.g., the original EQA-v1 baselines) lack local details and are vulnerable to ambiguity from complicated visual conditions, so both answering and navigation accuracy are poor.
motivation: EQA has broad applications (automatic driving, in-home robots, personal assistants). Global CNN features miss local semantic details such as objects and their attributes, which are needed for correct VQA answers and navigation.
key_idea: Extract local semantic features with a fast video segmentation framework, use them to drive a bottom-up visual attention for the VQA module, and fuse them into the navigator's training.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so the mechanism is not verifiable in detail. The abstract's ablations indicate that segmentation-derived local semantics improve VQA accuracy (68.99% vs 64.73%) and overall EQA accuracy (48.59% vs 44.98%). The feature fusion is reported to guide the navigator at little extra computational cost.
method: High-speed video segmentation framework: extracts local semantic features from the agent's video frames.
Bottom-up visual attention for VQA: uses the extracted semantic features to guide attention in the VQA sub-task.
Feature fusion strategy: fuses segmentation features to guide navigator training without much additional computational cost.

setting.backbone: EQA-style navigator (planner/controller) plus a VQA module with segmentation-based attention (details not given in the abstract)
setting.training_data: not stated in abstract (presumably EQA-v1 data)
